title: Marketplace inference value casebook: seller growth & trust use-cases
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This casebook equips sales and solutions engineers with a compact, repeatable story for marketplace customers (two‑sided platforms: buyers + sellers). It bundles positioning, competitive context, sample pricing scenarios, a one‑page pitch outline, a short customer case study, and a prospect-focused Security FAQ. Use this when: discovery surfaces seller-side personalization, automated moderation, fraud detection, or onboarding automation as top priorities.

Audience: GTM (AEs, SEs, AMs), solutions architects, and customer engineering.

Key thesis

- Marketplaces scale when seller activation, trust, and buyer-seller matching improve simultaneously.
- Inference controls the economics: latency and per-call cost directly affect throughput (conversions) and margin.
- Redwood’s differentiated offering: predictable SLO-backed serving, cost-aware controls (batching/quantization), and deployment flexibility (hosted/dedicated/private) reduces risk for platform teams.

Why marketplaces care (concise outcomes)

- Faster seller onboarding -> higher activation: automated intake + personalized recommendations reduce time-to-first-listing.
- Higher buyer conversion from personalized search/rank -> small latency wins compound to large revenue lifts.
- Trust & safety at scale -> automated moderation + reranking saves manual review costs and reduces fraud exposure.
- Unit economics clarity -> predictable per-transaction inference costs enable margin modelling for marketplace take rates.

Positioning and messaging (battle-tested lines)

Top-line positioning for pitches (3 variants depending on buyer):
- For Product/Marketplace PMs: "Make seller activation 2x faster while keeping latency under 150ms for search personalization — with predictable, auditable inference costs."
- For Engineering/Platform: "Replace brittle self-hosted inference pipelines with a single runtime that gives deterministic p99 latency, autoscaling, and can failover to cheaper model variants automatically."
- For Security/Legal: "Run inference where you need it: hosted for speed, dedicated for isolation, or Private/VPC for audited data paths and KMS integration."

Three-line elevator pitch (use in outreach):

"Redwood Inference helps marketplaces serve personalized results and seller automation with production-grade latency and cost controls. We give engineering teams predictable SLOs, built-in fallbacks, and the deployment options needed for regulated markets — so you can grow transactions without hidden inference costs."

Competitive brief (snapshot)

Objective: Provide a quick comparative frame for common objections. Keep this to one slide in a pitch.

Competitors compared: generic cloud managed endpoints, open-source self-hosted stacks, and single-vendor LLM API platforms.

| Capability | Redwood Inference | Cloud-managed endpoints | Self-hosted open stack | Single-vendor LLM API |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Predictable p99 latency (SLO) | Yes — SLA tiers | Varies | Depends on infra | Varies by model |
| Cost controls (batching/quantization) | Built-in, recommendations + Optimize toolkit | Manual tuning | Requires infra & infra-engineering | Limited |
| Private/VPC / On‑prem option | Yes (private control plane + on‑prem) | Limited | Yes (but heavy ops) | Rare |
| Rollouts + automatic fallback | Canary/A-B + model-variant fallback | Limited | Needs orchestration | Limited |
| Observability (token-level cost breakdown) | Yes | Basic | Custom | Limited |
| Time-to-production for new models | Days | Days–weeks | Weeks–months | Days |

Key rebuttals and scripts

- Objection: "We can host models ourselves, cheaper."
  Script: "Hosting looks cheaper until you add the engineering hours for kernel tuning, KV cache correctness, autoscaling for tail latency, and incident response. Redwood buys down that operational effort and gives you predictable economics you can model against transactions."

- Objection: "We can just use a public LLM API for prototypes."
  Script: "Public APIs are great for prototypes. For marketplaces, you need deterministic latency, data controls, and transparent per-token economics at scale — especially when inference cost becomes a meaningful line item in your unit economics."

Pricing guidance and example scenarios

Principles to convey during pricing conversations:
- Anchor to business metrics (e.g., lift in activation rate, conversion, or reviews processed) not tokens.
- Use a blended model for pilots: hosted API at usage-tiered rates -> move to Dedicated when sustained throughput increases predictability.
- Show the math: per‑transaction inference cost * transactions = monthly inference spend; provide suggestions to reduce unit cost (quantization, caching, lower-capacity variant for background jobs).

Representative pricing scenarios (simplified, for conversation only)

Assumptions: average inference call = 350 tokens (generation + context), marketplace handles 2M inference calls/month for personalization and onboarding automation.

Scenario A — Hosted (fast pilot):
- Price: $0.0008 per generate token (example anchor for sales) + $0.0003 per embed token for embedding calls.
- Monthly estimate: 2M calls * 350 tokens * $0.0008 = $560,000/month.
- Mitigations: Enable prefix caching for templates (expected 30% token reduction), use cheaper model for non-latency-sensitive workloads (reduce to $0.0004/token).
- Adjusted estimate: 560k * 0.7 * 0.5 = ~$196,000/month (pilot-optimized).

Scenario B — Dedicated (predictable throughput):
- Reserved capacity contract with committed monthly spend (example): $85k/month for a pool that comfortably serves 2M calls with p99 < 200ms.
- Added benefits: data isolation, predictable latency, lower unit cost when compared to peak-hosted pricing.

Scenario C — Private (regulatory / enterprise):
- Platform fee + support + infra requirement. Typical starts at $150k/year platform fee + infra costs; break-even often occurs when you require audited data paths and ~>X throughput where infra costs are internalized.

How to run a short pilot (3-week plan)

1. Week 0: Discovery & success metrics (activation lift %, p99 latency target, allowed cost per conversion). Owner: AE + SE.
2. Week 1: Pilot setup — decide hosted vs dedicated evaluation lane, small dataset onboarding, key prompts / templates. Owner: SE.
3. Week 2: Integration & monitoring — token-level cost dashboard, early quality evaluation (sample prompt sets), baseline A/B test. Owner: Customer Eng + SE.
4. Week 3: Demo results & conversion plan — show measured lift and economics, propose committed pricing or dedicated sizing. Owner: AE + AM.

Pitch deck outline (single-page / 5-slide quick deck)

Slide 1: Problem — friction in seller activation, moderation backlog, and conversion leakage. Include 1–2 data points.
Slide 2: Redwood solution — low-latency inference with cost controls and deployment flexibility.
Slide 3: Customer outcome — sample metrics (activation time down 40%, manual reviews down 70%).
Slide 4: Pricing & deployment options — hosted pilot estimate, Dedicated example, Private summary.
Slide 5: Next steps & pilot checklist (3-week plan).

One-page battlecard (talking points for SEs)

- Opening: "We help marketplaces keep search under 150ms p99 while reducing per-conversion inference spend."
- Tech advantage: runtime tuned for KV caching and continuous batching; automatic model fallback.
- Business angle: predictable inference spend that can be directly modeled into take-rate economics.
- Risk mitigation: private control plane for regulated sellers + KMS integration for per-tenant encryption keys.

Customer case study (anonymized composite): Marketly (fictional composite built from similar wins)

Context: Mid-market two-sided marketplace focusing on niche home services. Pain: Low seller activation and manual moderation backlog of 12k content items/month.
Approach: Pilot used hosted API for onboarding automation and an embeddings + rerank flow for search personalization. Implemented caching for onboarding templates and a dedicated low-cost model for background classification.
Outcomes (8 weeks post pilot):
- Time-to-first-active-seller reduced from 6 days to 1.8 days (70% improvement).
- Buyer search conversions improved by 14% (A/B test).
- Manual moderation workload reduced 62%, saving 0.6 FTE in triage labor (~$40k/year).
- After evaluation, Marketly moved high‑sensitivity workloads to Dedicated capacity with a 30% lower unit cost vs peak-hosted.

Security FAQ for marketplace prospects (short answers to accelerate conversations)

Q: Can we keep PII off Redwood logs?
A: Yes. We support customer-controlled request filtering and tokenization at the SDK layer and provide options to redact/omit PII before it reaches the control plane. For Private deployments, data stays in your VPC.

Q: How do you handle keys and encryption?
A: KMS integrations available (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM for Private customers. We support per-tenant encryption keys and key rotation policies.

Q: Is inference audited? Can we get request traces?
A: Yes. Audit logs include request metadata (no raw prompt bodies unless explicitly enabled). We provide configurable retention windows and can deliver exports for compliance reviews.

Q: What controls exist to prevent model drift or regressions?
A: Redwood Optimize integrates with evaluation harnesses and can run continuous evals on chosen prompt sets. Rollouts are gated with canaries, A/B, and automatic rollback on quality regressions.

Q: How is data residency handled?
A: Deployments can be region-locked. Hosted customers can select cloud-region endpoints; Dedicated/Private deployments allow full control over data residency.

Q: Can we run safe content filters and custom classifiers locally?
A: Yes. You can deploy dedicated classifiers to a private pool for sensitive moderation, or use mixed strategy: public-hosted for low-risk, private for escalations.

Operational targets & SLOs to propose in deals

- Latency: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 250ms (hosted tier sample)
- Availability: 99.9% for hosted API; SLA-backed higher tiers for Dedicated
- Cost variance guardrails: monthly unit-cost drift alert if spend-per-conversion changes > 15% quarter-over-quarter

Rollout checklist for SEs (go-to-production)

1. Agree success metrics and thresholds (conversion delta, latency SLO, allowed cost per active seller).
2. Establish data governance: what user data flows through inference, PII handling, retention windows.
3. Choose pilot deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated) and map infra requirements.
4. Instrument token-level cost dashboards and tracing.
5. Run initial A/B test for personalization or onboarding flow.
6. Evaluate results, propose Dedicated sizing or Private deployment if needed.

Appendix: Quick technical configuration table

| Item | Recommended config for Marketplace personalization pilot |
|---|---|
| Model family | Medium-latency open LLM or moderate-cost generation model |
| Max sequence length | 1024 tokens (truncate non-critical history) |
| Caching | Prefix + KV cache enabled for templates; TTL 24–72 hours |
| Batch size | Runtime auto-batching enabled; target latency budget p95 <= 120ms |
| Monitoring | Token-level cost, latency histograms, model-quality evals daily |
| Security | KMS integration, audit logs enabled, redact PII at ingestion |
